framework_notes: CACI is a defense IT-services / intel mission-support prime, not a hardware/PE-concentrated small-cap. The 10-K narrative is built on capability themes (SIGINT, EW, C-UAS, FSO/photonics, special operations support) and customer concentration (94.8% federal, 69.8% DoD), but does NOT cite specific Pentagon Program Elements, PE numbers, or named programs of record. Consequently the J-Book divergence pattern (named PE -> unfunded in latest J-Book) cannot be cleanly applied: the pentagon_jbook corpus (FY2026 J-Book, 410 PEs heavily seeded for emerging-tech/quantum/sUAS short cases) returns NOT_FOUND or NOT_FOUND_IN_TIMERANGE for the capability-level queries. The usaspending rear-view is overwhelmingly corroborative: CACI/CACI subs have $7.6B over 2,662 DoD awards (IPPS-A, DCSA background investigations, AFSCN, F3I-2 ISR), confirming the past revenue side of management's representations. The dominant scoring outcome is UNVERIFIABLE — not because the framework caught a divergence, but because CACI does not present claims that the J-Book mechanism is designed to verify. The control assertions (federal-revenue concentration, GSA/IDIQ vehicle mix, geographic mix) all PASS via the orthogonal sources.

scores.claim_text: CACI is at the forefront of developing free space optical (FSO) communications and long-range sensing using lasers, and acquired multi-domain photonics technologies for FSO communications during fiscal 2022.
scores.M_check: pentagon_jbook.query_program_funding (program_name='Free Space Optical Communications' | 'Optical Communications' | contractor_name='CACI')
scores.M_value: All three queries returned NOT_FOUND (no matching PE / program in the FY2026 J-Book corpus, no CACI primary-contractor program).
scores.interpretation: Corpus coverage gap. FSO/photonics work at CACI scale is funded through line items the v1 corpus does not enumerate (Space Force / Air Force RDT&E lines, classified IC budgets). Per rubric #7 (NOT_FOUND != red flag), this is a true UNVERIFIABLE — not evidence of divergence. The forward-looking capability claim is too generic to anchor to a single PE; in a hardened build the verifier would need IC-side J-Book extraction or DARPA/SDA program lookup, neither of which is in the v1 corpus.

scores.claim_text: CACI provides full-spectrum cyber, electronic warfare, and Counter-UAS solutions.
scores.M_value: Counter-UAS / Counter Unmanned Aircraft System: NOT_FOUND. Electronic Warfare: 3 matches (PE 0604270F Electronic Warfare Development, PE 0205671F Joint Counter RCIED EW, PE 0207040F Multi-Platform EW Equipment), all status=NOT_FOUND_IN_TIMERANGE because the corpus only carries FY2026 J-Book data, not the cutoff-FY2023 columns; status_declared and history_rows empty.
scores.interpretation: Capability-level claim, not program-element-level. The three EW PE matches are correctly retrieved by the corpus but cannot be evaluated at cutoff 2023-01-15 because the J-Book extraction is point-in-time FY2026 with no FY2023 history. Per rubric #1 NOT_FOUND_IN_TIMERANGE -> UNVERIFIABLE. No evidence that the underlying EW/C-UAS funding is being zeroed; this is a corpus capability gap, not a CACI red flag.

scores.claim_text: CACI delivers multi-domain SIGINT, resilient communications, FSO, EW, cyber ops, and 5G/RF spectrum capabilities.
scores.M_value: Signals Intelligence: NOT_FOUND. SIGINT: 1 match (PE 0304260F Airborne SIGINT Enterprise, Air Force, status=NOT_FOUND_IN_TIMERANGE, no history rows). 5G: NOT_FOUND.
scores.interpretation: The single SIGINT PE match is again FY2026-J-Book-only; no cutoff-FY2023 funding history is available. The 'multi-domain SIGINT' claim is far broader than any single PE — CACI's IC-side work is overwhelmingly classified-customer (NSA/NRO/CIA) which sits outside the public J-Book exhibits. UNVERIFIABLE by corpus design.

scores.claim_text: CACI acquired Ascent Vision Technologies (AVT) in fiscal 2021 for EO/IR + Computer Vision + C-UAS — positioning on DoD C-UAS programs.
scores.M_check: pentagon_jbook.query_program_funding (contractor='Ascent Vision' | program='Counter-Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems') + usaspending.query_dod_contracts(recipient='Ascent Vision Technologies')
scores.M_value: Pentagon J-Book: NOT_FOUND for both AVT contractor lookup and C-sUAS program lookup. USAspending: AVT has only 1 standalone DoD award totaling $244,244.77 (Marine Corps software-support contract M6785420C0004, pre-acquisition), confirming AVT was a tiny pre-acquisition prime — its DoD revenue post-acquisition flows through CACI legal entities.
scores.interpretation: AVT was acquired for capability, not for an existing DoD contract base. The C-UAS program-of-record exposure post-2021 would appear under CACI parent legal entities in USAspending (not searchable as 'Ascent Vision'). No J-Book divergence detectable. Per rubric #6 partial: USAspending shows the prior contracts side is consistent (small pre-acq); J-Book NOT_FOUND for C-sUAS suggests corpus coverage gap, not a real defunded program. UNVERIFIABLE.

scores.claim_text: DoD = 69.8% of FY2022 revenue (94.8% federal total). CACI expects federal government contracts to remain primary revenue source.
scores.M_value: usaspending DoD: 2,662 DoD awards totaling $7,619,067,209.36 across CACI legal entities (CACI-ISS LLC IPPS-A $734M, CACI Inc-Federal DCSA Background-Investigation Fieldwork $652M, CACI NSS LLC AFSCN $601M and F3I-2 ISR $578M, CACI Premier Technology background-investigations $577M). Federal-presence resolves to 7 UEIs under the CACI parent. FY-snapshot top entity (CACI International Inc, UEI QSRTXLFKV857) carrying $4.48B.
scores.interpretation: Customer-concentration claim is fully corroborated by USAspending — CACI is in fact a multi-billion-dollar DoD prime. No divergence between claim and verifier. PASS.

scores.claim_text: Top-10 contracts = 35.7% / $2.2B of FY2022 revenue, many comprising multiple task orders.
scores.M_value: Top awards visible (IPPS-A $734M, DCSA background-investigation TO $652M, AFSCN $601M, F3I-2 ISR $578M, DCSA background TO $577M); these alone exceed $3.1B obligated and align with a top-10 portfolio in the $2.2B annual-revenue range when amortized across multi-year periods of performance.
scores.interpretation: Concentration figure ($2.2B / 35.7%) is consistent with the visible award stack. PASS.

scores.claim_text: CACI provides special operations services (incl. counterterrorism training) and intelligence/special operations mission support.
scores.M_value: Both queries returned NOT_FOUND. The corpus is seeded for emerging-tech / quantum / sUAS / autonomy short cases, not SOCOM operating budget lines.
scores.interpretation: Capability-level claim outside the v1 J-Book corpus scope (SOCOM mission-support lines not enumerated). Per rubric #7, NOT_FOUND treated as UNVERIFIABLE rather than red flag.

scores.claim_text: Domestic Operations = 96.9% of FY2022 revenue (geographic mix control claim).
scores.M_value: edgar_fts returned 0 hits (FTS index does not surface this 10-K's segment language for the search term used).
scores.interpretation: Control claim, not load-bearing on the J-Book thesis. Geographic mix is internally consistent with the segment description but cannot be independently re-verified by edgar_fts under the chosen search term. Non-material. UNVERIFIABLE.

scores.claim_text: 8 acquisitions over FY2020-FY2022 to add OSINT, SATCOM, FSO/photonics, CSfC, EO/IR, C-UAS capabilities — rollup thesis.
scores.M_value: Scorer returned coherence_score=0.0 for all five entries, all labeled 'low_coherence' with reasoning 'no target name / business description provided.' The 10-K names AVT (FY2021) explicitly but the four FY2022 acquisitions are described only by capability (photonics/FSO, CSfC, OSINT, SATCOM) without target names.
scores.interpretation: The 10-K's deliberate non-naming of the FY2022 acquisitions defeats the acq_coherence verifier — the framework cannot grade individual deals without targets. AVT alone is a clearly-coherent C-UAS/EO-IR fit. The thesis is plausible but the verifier is starved. UNVERIFIABLE; would benefit from cross-checking M&A 8-K disclosures filed FY2022 (separate workflow, outside this run).

scores.claim_text: CACI sells extensively through GSA schedules and other GWAC/IDIQ vehicles.
scores.M_check: edgar_fts.query_fulltext(cik=0000016058, search_term='GSA IDIQ task order', cutoff_date=2023-01-15)
scores.M_value: edgar_fts returned 0 total hits. The FTS index for CIK 0000016058 with this search term did not surface filings.
scores.interpretation: Control claim, not J-Book-grounded. Search term may be too specific; the claim is itself consistent with the visible USAspending award descriptions (most CACI awards are task orders under IDIQ ceilings). UNVERIFIABLE under chosen query but not contradicted by any source.

summary.framework_self_assessment: This is a NULL-RESULT cohort observation for the J-Book divergence pattern. The framework correctly avoided false positives: CACI does not exhibit the canonical YSS/IONQ short pattern (no named PE concentration), the verifier returned UNVERIFIABLE rather than RED_FLAG on capability-level claims, and the orthogonal verifier (USAspending) corroborated the load-bearing customer-concentration claims. To convert UNVERIFIABLE -> actionable on CACI-class targets the framework would need: (a) IC-side budget extraction (NIP/MIP), (b) FY2023 J-Book historical columns, (c) SOCOM operating-budget exhibits, (d) GWAC/IDIQ ceiling-vs-obligation tracker.
